item.title: Ouchijuku: A Frozen-in-Time Edo Post Town & Negi Soba — Guide
item.description: Ouchijuku is a beautifully preserved Edo-period post town, its single main street lined with thatched-roof buildings that once served travellers on the old Aizu-Nishi Kaido route between Aizu and Nikko. Today the village is a living museum of traditional rural Japan, with shops selling crafts and local food. Its most famous quirk is negi-soba — buckwheat noodles eaten using a single whole green onion (negi) instead of chopsticks, a tradition unique to Ouchijuku.
